journey.title: Request details and troubleshooting
journey.subtitle: Correlate the matched route, trace and token records by Trace ID. Refresh and edit preparation only read records; a real request is resent only after explicit execution confirmation.
journey.replayPrepareHint: Load the captured request for editing without sending it.
journey.replayUnavailable: No editable request was captured, or this request explicitly does not support replay. Resending is unavailable.
journey.replayIdentityMismatch: The prepared data does not match this request. Resending was blocked. Close the editor and refresh before trying again.
journey.replayPrepareError: Could not prepare the request. No request was sent.
journey.replayExecuteError: Could not confirm the resend result. The request may already have executed; verify the outcome before sending again.
journey.replayFailed: The resend was unsuccessful. Check the response and error details.
journey.confirmOriginalTitle: Resend the original request without edits?
journey.resendWarning: This sends a real request and may cause side effects and Token charges.
journey.resendWarningDetail: Verify the target route, credentials and payload. Execution may duplicate writes or trigger business operations. Closing or leaving this page after sending does not mean server execution is cancelled.
journey.httpClue: HTTP status mappings provide preliminary clues, not confirmed causes. A status code alone cannot establish an authentication failure or an upstream root cause; verify the response, filter records and advanced trace.
journey.notAi: Regular request: AI token metering does not apply
journey.routeMismatch: The request matched a different route. Check the path, method and route priority.
journey.routeUnavailable: The current route is unavailable or deleted. Existing request evidence remains available.
journey.advice.pending: Records arrive asynchronously; this page briefly polls for them. If none appear, check reporting connectivity, internal credentials and persistent queues.
journey.result.traceMissing: Usage found; trace not found yet
journey.advice.traceMissing: The trace may be delayed, unsampled or expired. This does not mean the request did not execute. Refresh later or reproduce using the debugger.
journey.result.usageMissing: Trace found; AI usage not found yet
journey.advice.usageMissing: Refresh shortly. If usage remains absent, check whether the request predates automatic metering and whether the reporting queue is backed up.
journey.advice.authentication: Authentication or authorization is a possible lead, not a confirmed cause. Identify which layer returned the response, then verify route policies and credential validity and scope.
journey.advice.rateLimit: A rate or quota limit is a possible lead. Verify the response source, then check route policies, tenant quotas and token windows before retrying.
journey.advice.routing: Use the trace to determine whether the gateway or upstream returned 404. Check the path, method, StripPrefix and matched route; a 404 alone does not establish a routing error.
journey.advice.upstream: A status code alone does not establish an upstream failure. Verify the error type, response and failing layer before checking endpoints, health, timeouts and provider status.
journey.advice.request: Request or business validation is a possible lead. Verify the response and filter records before checking the model, body and content security policy; do not assume a root cause.
journey.advice.settlement: Inspect the usage ledger and settlement status. Allow automatic recovery before applying a verified manual correction.
journey.advice.usageUnknown: Check stream interruption, provider usage reporting and response format. Unknown usage is not zero; reconcile using provider evidence.
journey.advice.ok: Inspect trace and usage details, or return to route configuration and manually send the next verification request.
